thesis: Confirmed fiscal Q4 2026 issuer results showed unaudited GMV of $14.1 billion (+36% year over year), revenue of $1.166 billion (+33%), and GAAP operating income of $147.3 million. The strongest counter-evidence is that $1.617 billion of GAAP net income included a $1.448 billion income-tax benefit; that distorts headline net income but does not negate the GMV and revenue growth or positive GAAP operating income, so the evidence supports a long read.
invalidation: A subsequent issuer filing shows material credit deterioration, reverses positive GAAP operating income, or materially weakens GMV and revenue growth without an offsetting improvement in transaction economics.

thesis: Confirmed Q2 2026 issuer results showed revenue of $268.5 million (+8.6% year over year), GAAP operating income of $12.4 million versus a prior-year loss, and a raised full-year outlook. However, the current volume spike is contemporaneous with the announced S&P SmallCap 600 addition effective August 31, a mechanical index event rather than fresh operating evidence; the operating improvement supports a long read, but the signal's mechanical character keeps conviction low.
invalidation: Full-year guidance is reduced, GAAP operating income reverses, or revenue growth weakens without an offsetting improvement in operating leverage.
sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices addition announcement: https://press.spglobal.com/2026-08-26-Tenable-Holdings-Set-to-Join-S-P-SmallCap-600

thesis: Confirmed fiscal 2026 issuer results showed record total revenue of $11.154 billion, rental-revenue growth of 3.4%, net income of $1.325 billion, and company-defined free cash flow of $2.055 billion, alongside the completed $650 million Reliant acquisition. The strongest counter-evidence is the material debt-classification correction that the July proxy identified as an accounting restatement; although it did not affect prior periods or executive compensation, that governance history and the absence of a fresh operating catalyst behind the volume spike keep the otherwise constructive long read at low conviction.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 2027 shows negative rental-revenue growth, materially weaker cash generation, or another material financial-reporting control error.
sources: Philadelphia Indemnity v. Sunbelt Rentals docket: https://dockets.justia.com/docket/washington/wawdce/2%3A2026cv01956/363774

thesis: The confirmed unaudited Q2 2026 issuer results are mixed: GTV increased 6.3% and net income increased 100.8%, while net revenue fell 5.7% and operating-expense improvement partly reflected cost optimization and lower headcount. The transaction-volume and profit gains suggest operating resilience, but revenue contraction and reliance on a leaner cost base keep the long read low-conviction.
invalidation: GTV turns negative or revenue contraction persists while margin and net-income improvement fades.

thesis: Confirmed Q2 fiscal 2027 results showed subscription ARR growth of 33%, revenue growth of 38%, positive operating cash flow of $76.8 million, and raised full-year guidance. The strongest counter-evidence is the ongoing DOJ matter disclosed in the 2026 Form 10-K: a former sales employee was indicted and Rubrik found employee communications tied to potential federal-contracting violations; growth and cash generation support a long read, but the qualifying governance history keeps conviction low.
invalidation: Subscription ARR or revenue growth slows materially, full-year guidance is reduced, operating cash flow turns negative, or the DOJ matter expands into charges or sanctions against Rubrik.
